when_to_say: Used to express gratitude in informal settings.
example: ありがとう、手伝ってくれて！ (arigatou, tetsudatte kurete!) - Thank you for helping me!

when_to_say: Standard greeting during daytime hours.
example: こんにちは、お元気ですか？ (konnichiwa, ogenki desu ka?) - Hello, how are you?

when_to_say: Used when leaving for a long period or permanently.
example: また明日、さようなら！ (mata ashita, sayounara!) - See you tomorrow, goodbye!

when_to_say: Used to agree or respond affirmatively.
example: はい、わかりました。 (hai, wakarimashita.) - Yes, I understood.

when_to_say: Used to disagree or refuse.
example: いいえ、違います。 (iie, chigaimasu.) - No, that's wrong.

when_to_say: Used to get someone's attention or apologize mildly.
example: すみません、時間を教えてください。 (sumimasen, jikan o oshiete kudasai.) - Excuse me, please tell me the time.

when_to_say: Used to offer a personal apology.
example: 遅れてごめんなさい。 (okurete gomen nasai.) - I am sorry for being late.

when_to_say: Used when enjoying food or drinks.
example: このラーメンはおいしいです。 (kono raamen wa oishii desu.) - This ramen is delicious.

when_to_say: Used to indicate the action of eating food.
example: 朝ごはんをたべる。 (asagohan o taberu.) - Eat breakfast.

when_to_say: Used when consuming liquids.
example: 水をのむ。 (mizu o nomu.) - Drink water.

when_to_say: Used to refer to a friend or acquaintance.
example: 彼は私のともだちです。 (kare wa watashi no tomodachi desu.) - He is my friend.

when_to_say: Used when referring to an educational institution.
example: 毎日がっこうに行きます。 (mainichi gakkou ni ikimasu.) - I go to school every day.

when_to_say: Used to address teachers, doctors, or experts.
example: 日本語のせんせい。 (nihongo no sensei.) - Japanese language teacher.

when_to_say: Used when referring to reading material or books.
example: 面白いほんを読んでいる。 (omoshiroi hon o yonde iru.) - I am reading an interesting book.

when_to_say: Used when something is challenging to do or solve.
example: この問題はむずかしい。 (kono mondai wa muzukashii.) - This problem is difficult.

when_to_say: Used to describe something simple or a person who is kind.
example: 彼女はとてもやさしい人です。 (kanojo wa totemo yasashii hito desu.) - She is a very kind person.

when_to_say: Used to ask for the price of something.
example: これはいくらですか？ (kore wa ikura desu ka?) - How much is this?

when_to_say: Used to ask for a location.
example: 駅はどこですか？ (eki wa doko desu ka?) - Where is the station?

when_to_say: Used when referring to the present moment.
example: いま何時ですか？ (ima nanji desu ka?) - What time is it now?

when_to_say: Used when referring to an electric train.
example: でんしゃで通勤します。 (densha de tsuukin shimasu.) - I commute by train.

when_to_say: Used when the climate or object is hot.
example: 今日はとてもあついです。 (kyou wa totemo atsui desu.) - Today is very hot.

when_to_say: Used to express cold climate condition.
example: 冬はさむいです。 (fuyu wa samui desu.) - Winter is cold.

when_to_say: Used when asking for cold or room-temperature drinking water.
example: みずをください。 (mizu o kudasai.) - Water, please.

when_to_say: Used when pointing to or discussing cats.
example: かわいいねこがいます。 (kawaii neko ga imasu.) - There is a cute cat.

when_to_say: Used when referring to dogs.
example: いぬと散歩する。 (inu to sanpo suru.) - Take a walk with the dog.

when_to_say: Used when talking about workplace.
example: かいしゃに行きます。 (kaisha ni ikimasu.) - I am going to the company.

when_to_say: Used to discuss professional duties.
example: 今日のしごとは終わりました。 (kyou no shigoto wa owarimashita.) - Today's work is finished.

when_to_say: Used when talking about academic or skill studies.
example: 日本語のべんきょうをします。 (nihongo no benkyou o shimasu.) - I study Japanese.

when_to_say: Used to refer to days off or resting moments.
example: 明日はやすみです。 (ashita wa yasumi desu.) - Tomorrow is a day off.

when_to_say: Used when asking or talking about duration and time.
example: じかんがありません。 (jikan ga arimasen.) - I don't have time.

when_to_say: Used when referring to one's family members.
example: かぞくを愛しています。 (kazoku o aishite imasu.) - I love my family.

when_to_say: Polite form to refer to someone else's or one's own mother.
example: おかあさんは料理が得意です。 (okaasan wa ryouri ga tokui desu.) - Mother is good at cooking.

when_to_say: Polite form to refer to a father.
example: おとうさんは会社員です。 (otousan wa kaishain desu.) - Father is a company employee.

when_to_say: Used when talking about rooms inside a house or hotel.
example: 私のへやは広いです。 (watashi no heya wa hiroi desu.) - My room is spacious.

when_to_say: Used to describe a residence.
example: いえに帰ります。 (ie ni kaerimasu.) - I am returning home.

when_to_say: Used when talking about early daytime.
example: あさ散歩をします。 (asa sanpo o shimasu.) - I take a walk in the morning.

when_to_say: Used when referring to nighttime.
example: よる10時に寝ます。 (yoru juuji ni nemasu.) - I sleep at 10 PM at night.

when_to_say: Used to talk about events happening on the current day.
example: きょうは天気が良いです。 (kyou wa tenki ga yoi desu.) - The weather is good today.

when_to_say: Used when referring to the day after today.
example: あした会いましょう。 (ashita aimashou.) - Let's meet tomorrow.

when_to_say: Used when talking about past events on the previous day.
example: きのう映画を見ました。 (kinou eiga o mimashita.) - Yesterday I watched a movie.

when_to_say: Used when going out to purchase items.
example: デパートへかいものに行く。 (depaato e kaimono ni iku.) - Go to the department store for shopping.

when_to_say: Used when talking about automobiles.
example: 新しいくるまを買いました。 (atarashii kuruma o kaimashita.) - I bought a new car.

when_to_say: Used when referring to air travel.
example: ひこうきで日本へ行きます。 (hikouki de nihon e ikimasu.) - I go to Japan by airplane.

when_to_say: Used when referring to medical facilities.
example: 具合が悪いのでびょういんに行きます。 (guai ga warui node byouin ni ikimasu.) - I feel unwell so I am going to the hospital.

when_to_say: Used when taking or buying medication.
example: 食後にくすりをのんでください。 (shokugo ni kusuri o nonde kudasai.) - Please take medicine after meals.

when_to_say: Used to describe writing code for software development.
example: 私はプログラミングを学んでいます。 (watashi wa puroguramingu o manande imasu.) - I am learning programming.

when_to_say: Used when referring to PC or digital computing devices.
example: 新しいコンピュータを買いたい。 (atarashii konpyuuta o kaitai.) - I want to buy a new computer.

when_to_say: Used when expressing future ambitions or time ahead.
example: みらいの目標を立てる。 (mirai no mokuhyou o tateru.) - Set goals for the future.

when_to_say: Used when talking about dreams during sleep or life aspirations.
example: 私のゆめはエンジニアになることです。 (watashi no yume wa enjiniai ni naru koto desu.) - My dream is to become an engineer.

when_to_say: Used when expressing accomplishment or achievement.
example: プロジェクトのせいこうを祈ります。 (purojekuto no seikou o inorimasu.) - I pray for the success of the project.
